messages:
kari: noticed a spike of session revokes for a small set of accounts in eu-west starting ~22:10 UTC, sessions bounce between active and revoked within seconds, lots of MFA prompts on same users :eyes:
kari: this looks like 'session flapping' not a normal brute force — device_fingerprint and user agent are identical across events
ben: sec-bot alerted 22:12, pointing to SSO_SESSION_FLAP rule with 48 events in 2m
sec-bot: alert: SSO_SESSION_FLAP - 48 matches, severity medium, affected_users: 7, top_ip: 85.214.33.12, runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/sso-flap
indra: any configuration changes around RBAC or token lifetime today?
kari: no RBAC pushes in last 24h from git history, deploys list clean. I grep'd audit-log for rc:role-modify and nothing.
maria: noticed KMS key-rotate job for the service-account that signs SSO tokens ran at 22:09 UTC — initial hypothesis: short-lived token signing key rotated but some nodes didn't pick up, causing temporary rejects and retries?
ben: if that's true we'd expect KMS audit entries. maria, can you post the KMS audit request ids?
maria: grabbing now, one sec.
sec-bot: k8s-deploy-bot: rolling update for auth-proxy started 21:58 and finished 22:02 - no errors reported.
maria: KMS logs show a rotate_call at 22:09 with request_id: kms-req-48321 but there are 503s from two kms-proxy instances around 22:09-22:11
indra: that aligns with session rejects then re-issues. If some auth nodes failed to fetch new public key, they'd reject tokens and trigger re-auth. Could cause MFA fatigue.
kari: good catch. For containment, can we throttle MFA prompts or temporarily extend token validity to avoid re-prompt storm while we fix key distribution?
enstreet: (sre-oncall) we should not extend token validity blindly, risk stale key exposure. Suggest: 1) block the culprit IP 85.214.33.12 at edge, 2) ensure all auth proxies reloaded keys, 3) run a forced key-sync and confirm via /internal/keys endpoint.
ben: I'm on (1) now. Adding ip block to edge WAF and firewall rules.
ben: blocked 85.214.33.12 at 22:18 UTC on WAF :white_check_mark:
sre-oncall: starting key-sync: kubectl exec -n auth svc/auth-proxy -- curl -sS localhost:8080/internal/reload-keys || true
sre-oncall: logs show successful sync on 3/4 pods; one pod was OOM-killed during the rotate window. K8s node 7 had transient disk pressure.
maria: restarted the pod and rechecked KMS fetches — all pods now report key version v2026-03-20-01 and no 503s in the last 5m
indra: great. Next: we need to check if any tokens minted with old keys were accepted incorrectly or if refresh loop caused account lockouts. Kari, can you surface list of affected users for comms?
kari: list exported to incident ticket INC-1989 with PII redacted, sending to sec-oncall and support leads.
ben: PRD incident page created and triage channel #incident-1989. Adding timeline and actions.
indra: asks for KMS audit entries for rotate_call + failed fetches, and whether KMS proxy returns 503 due to quota or connection issue. Need follow-up with infra to check node disk pressure root cause.
maria: filing infra ticket INFRA-2456 about disk pressure and OOMs. Also raising KMS SLA investigation with cloud team — initial evidence points to transient proxy failures, not secret compromise.
kari: comms draft for affected customers: short note about transient re-auth prompts and lockouts while we rotated keys; recommend passwordless tokens unaffected. Draft posted in ticket for review.
ben: action items assigned: ben -> WAF block done; sre-oncall -> pod restart and key-sync done; maria -> KMS audit export and cloud ticket; indra -> RBAC config audit and rollback check; kari -> customer comms and closure note.
sec-bot: incident severity updated to low after containment 22:25 UTC. Postmortem requested with DRI assigned to indra, due in 72h.
indra: postmortem should include: timeline, KMS logs, why one pod got OOM, how key distribution is validated, and a test to verify zero-downtime key rotations (maybe prefetch new key before switching).
kari: also adding a short-term mitigation: add health-check on /internal/keys and alert if fetch fails 3x in 1m.
maria: question for security/compliance — do we need to mark this as a KMS-integrity incident requiring audit export to compliance? current thought: no PII exposure, no auth bypass, but we should preserve KMS audit and token mint logs for 90 days.
indra: agree preserve logs; tag incident INC-1989 and sync with legal if customers reported lockouts.
ben: summary: not an attack, operational failure during key rotate causing session flapping and MFA fatigue, contained by blocking IP, restarting pod, forcing key sync, and preserving audit logs. Postmortem DRI indra.
kari: closing notes: will follow up with runbook updates for key rotation checklist and add automated key prefetch. Thanks all :pray:
